title: I-35W bridge: gusset-plate design error, added loads, and inspection/load-rating invisibility
summary: I-35W is encoded as a bridge-load-path and governance record: an underdesigned gusset-plate condition was not caught by design review, inspection, or load-rating practice, then was stressed by dead-load increases and construction loads.

status_history.note: Added as civil/structural failure lane record.

claims.claim: The NTSB investigation page records that the I-35W deck truss bridge collapsed on August 1, 2007, during rush hour, with construction loads on the bridge, causing 13 deaths and 145 injuries.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB probable-cause statement attributes the collapse to inadequate load capacity caused by a design error in the U10 gusset plates, with previous weight increases and construction loads contributing.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB also identifies failures in quality-control/design-review procedures and inadequate attention to gusset plates in inspections and load ratings.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The record is encoded as a hidden critical-member/design-review and inspection/load-rating visibility case rather than merely an overload case.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.system: steel deck truss bridge, gusset plates, load rating, inspection and construction-load controls

sequence_of_events.event: Bridge entered service with under-capacity U10 gusset plates due to a design error.
Additional dead load accumulated over service life.
Construction materials/equipment added load during deck work.
Bridge collapsed, and NTSB traced design review, inspection, and load-rating visibility failures.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Inadequate load capacity of U10 gusset plates under combined loads.
contributing_factors: gusset plates not adequately addressed in inspections and load ratings
latent_conditions: critical connection/member assumptions not explicit in routine bridge-management surfaces
inspection and load-rating standards did not force sufficient review of gusset plates in this case
construction-load governance did not compensate for hidden design-margin error

structural_factor_axes.inspection_axis: inspection/load-rating failed to identify critical-member capacity issue
structural_factor_axes.correction_surface: NTSB investigation and infrastructure safety recommendations
